label: Essential truth: it lies in the nature of x that φ (Fine's box-sub-x), a primitive
term: essential truth of a being (the Essential parameter)
definition: Essential x φ, for a being x and a world-proposition φ over the frame's points: it lies in the nature of x that φ (Fine's □ₓ φ). A primitive Lean parameter of type B → (W → Prop) → Prop of TruthCore.Modal.ModalGrounding, constrained only by the premises that use it: essence grounds necessity (EssenceGroundsNecessity: an essential truth holds at every accessible world), the essentialist account of possibility (EssentialExclusionAccount), existence-conditional essences (ExistenceConditionalEssences: every essential truth about x holds wherever x is absent) and unconditional essentialism's reading of esse = essence (EsseEssenceIsEssentialExistence). A related helper is defined: EntailsExistence F φ x, φ entails x's existence over every point of the frame's world type.
note: Stipulated for #1887 (docs/notes/modal-grounding-frameworks.md). Examples: it lies in the nature of a singleton that it has its member; of water that it is H2O. Non-examples: that Socrates is a member of his singleton is necessary but does not lie in Socrates' nature (Fine 1994's point against the modal analysis of essence; navigation only); that a contingent being happens to exist at w. Distinct from necessity (essence implies necessity under EssenceGroundsNecessity, not conversely), from CAUSE_2 and from POWER_OVER_ESSE_1. Structural properties assumed: none. Distinct from the existing EssenceReasonSeparation.Profile.InEssence, which represents only existence facts in essences and so cannot state an existence-conditional essence; the two are not related by any bridge. Senses of 'essence' in DISAMB-ESSENCE (Scott, Godel, q.3 a.4 essenceOf) are different notions: here essenceOf/esseOf remain the q.3 a.4 represented essence and esse, and Essential is the Finean nature-relative truth; the only bridge between them is the explicit OPEN premise EsseEssenceIsEssentialExistence. Open obligations: whether an esse-essence identity is a case of existence belonging to an essence (the Kant-type thesis, the decisive question in docs/notes/foundational-absence-warrant.md). What would source it: Fine, 'Essence and Modality' (1994); Lowe, 'Two Notions of Being' (2008).
